subject: Pricing bucket qualification + procurement thresholds (post-demo)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: connor.obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + numbers we discussed (Redwood demo)

Jared — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Wanted to capture the key items and next steps while they’re fresh.

Call recap (short):
- Use case: realtime customer support summarization + intent routing for ~50M monthly messages (ingest) but only ~3–5% generate completions.
- Expected token profile: avg prompt 120 tokens, avg gen 220 tokens (conservative estimate).
- Estimated monthly tokens (rough): 50M messages * 0.04 * (120+220) ≈ 680M tokens/month.
- Target unit economics you mentioned in the call: ballpark target $/1M tokens in the range $12–$25 depending on latency and SLA.

What I need from you to finalize the pricing band conversation:
1) Confirm whether the 50M messages is a steady state or peak month.
2) Procurement threshold: will your procurement team require a PO/commit bracket if monthly spend exceeds $10k/$25k/$100k?
3) Any legal constraints on contract length or auto-renewal we should be aware of before we prepare a committed-capacity quote.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm (1)-(3) above by EOD Monday.
- I’ll put together two options: a) pay-as-you-go with dynamic routing + suggested batching settings, and b) a 12-month committed capacity band (three tiers) with target $/1M tokens aligned to your $/1M target ranges.

I’ve attached a one-page pricing sketch (redwood-pricing-1Mtokens.xlsx) showing how the $/1M changes at 1M/50M/500M token bands and the estimated monthly spend given your current numbers.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers we discussed (Redwood demo)

Thanks, Hannah — short answers below and a couple of clarifications from procurement.

1) 50M messages is our steady-state estimate for Q2/Q3 next year; we expect a ramp (pilot -> prod) over 3 months. Peak month could be ~1.8x steady-state.
2) Procurement note: spend-based PO thresholds — anything below $10k/month we can handle via credit card + standard SOW. Between $10k–$50k/month requires a Purchase Order + 30-day net payment; over $50k/month triggers our procurement committee review and likely a master services agreement. We prefer annual commitments but will accept quarterly billing for pilots.
3) No unusual legal constraints — standard indemnities and export controls only. We will want SOC2 evidence and a data handling blurb in the SOW.

Given the numbers: if the conservative 680M tokens/month estimate holds, at $12/1M tokens that’s ~$8,160/month; at $25/1M tokens that’s ~$17,000/month. Procurement thinks $10k+/month will need formal PO — so we’d likely start with a pilot at a lower committed band and scale.

We’ve attached a procurement requirements summary (acme-procurement-req.pdf).

— Jared
Jared Lowe
Head of Product Integrations | Acme Analytics
jared.lowe@acmeanalytics.com
Attachment: acme-procurement-req.pdf

Thanks for the clarifications, Jared — very helpful. I pasted the procurement thresholds below and added proposed commercial fit + immediate ask.

Procurement thresholds (per your note):
- < $10k/month: credit card / SOW OK
- $10k–$50k/month: PO + 30-day net
- > $50k/month: procurement committee / MSA review

Commercial fit / recommendation (high level):
- Pilot option (90 days): commit to a 10M token cushion (pay-as-you-go beyond), target price $28/1M tokens, monthly cap at $8k. This keeps procurement in CC-free zone and minimizes legal overhead.
- Committed band (12 months): three tiers we will propose — Tier A (50–200M tokens/mo), Tier B (200–700M tokens/mo), Tier C (700M+ tokens/mo). At each tier we can step the $/1M down substantially; as an example, Tier B target is $14–18/1M tokens depending on latency SLO and KV caching.

Immediate ask for procurement team: please confirm whether Acme can sign a 12-month committed band with quarterly invoicing and 30-day terms. If not, we’ll prepare a pilot-focused SOW.

Action items assigned:
- Jared: confirm pilot vs immediate committed band preference by EOD Wednesday (Nov 4).
- Connor (internal): can you draft the committed-band term sheet and a pilot SOW variant? I’ve looped Monica for SOC2 and security evidence.

If it helps, I’ll also include a worked example showing monthly spend at 680M tokens vs a 1.8x peak so procurement sees the delta.

Hannah
